items.description: The Essex coast from Clacton to and including, St Peters Flat and the Colne and Blackwater estuaries
items.message:
High tides this evening may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 00:45am to 2:45am on Friday 13 November.
Clacton Promenade, Lee-over-Sands and Brightlingsea sea front may see some wave overtopping and spray. The Strood at Mersea Island, Coast Road and car parks on the front at West Mersea, and the Hythe and Promenade at Maldon may be flooded. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Clacton of 2.71mAODN at 1:45am on Friday 13 November, which is 0.61m above tide tables, Wind Force 5, north westerly. No further high tides are expected over the coming days.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Friday 13 November or as the situation changes.

items.message:

Locations most affected will be Coalhouse Fort and car park, and the low lying land between the fort and Coalhouse Point. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at  Southend of 3.50mAODN at 2:30pm, on Thursday 12 November, which is 0.75m above tide tables, Wind Force 5, Northerly. No further high tides are expected over the coming days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 4:00PM on Thursday 12 November or as the situation changes.

High tides and forecast weather conditions throughout the evening may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 5:45pm to 9:45pm on Thursday 12 November. 
Locations most affected will be low-lying land and roads near rivers or on the coast, with spray being seen on the seafront paths. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. Please take notice of the Flood Sign at top of South Beach Road. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at King's Lynn of 3.86mAODN at 7:45pm on 12 November, which is 0.6m above tide tables, Wind Force 6, Northerly. No further high tides are expected over the coming days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 9:30AM on Friday 13 November or as the situation changes.

items.description: Tidal Thames riverside from Putney Bridge to Teddington Weir
items.eaAreaName: Kent, South London and East Sussex

floodArea.county: Greater London, Hammersmith and Fulham, Hounslow, Richmond upon Thames, Wandsworth

items.message:
High tides today may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM on 12/11/2026. 
The forecast high tide at Richmond is 4.74 mAOD at 4:00 PM on Thursday 12th November.

Locations most affected will be Putney Embankment (SW15), Chiswick Mall and Strand on the Green (W4), Thames Bank at Mortlake (SW14), Ranelagh Drive (TW1), Friars Lane and Water Lane (TW9), Riverside and The Embankment at Twickenham, and the Towpath below Teddington Lock. Flooding of properties is not expected.

Astronomical tide levels are falling. The river flow at Teddington Weir is 5 cubic metres per second and is steady. We anticipate the flows to remain steady for the next few days. 
We are closing flood gates . 
Avoid using low lying footpaths and any bridges near local watercourses.   
This message will be updated by 5:30PM on Thursday 12 November or as the situation changes.
